cls: HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI, antiretroviral)
pharm: A second-generation HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor that binds the active site of HIV-1 integrase and blocks the strand-transfer step of retroviral DNA integration into the host genome, preventing formation of the HIV provirus and viral replication, with a high barrier to resistance.
quick: 50 mg once daily; 50 mg twice daily if INSTI resistance or with certain UGT/CYP3A inducers
May be taken with or without food; take with food if given with certain INSTI-resistance
Effective in pregnancy; discuss a small periconception neural-tube-defect signal and folate
In HIV, breastfeeding generally not recommended in high-resource settings; follow local guidance
No adjustment for mild-severe impairment; not studied in dialysis
No adjustment in mild-moderate (Child-Pugh A/B); not recommended in severe (C)
Hypersensitivity/hepatic reactions, LFTs (esp. with hepatitis co-infection), HIV RNA/CD4, weight
summary: Dolutegravir is a second-generation HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) used, in combination with other antiretrovirals, to treat HIV-1 infection in adults and children, and is a backbone of many first-line regimens because of its potency, once-daily dosing, and high genetic barrier to resistance. It blocks integration of viral DNA into host DNA. Key safety issues are hypersensitivity reactions (which can include rash, constitutional symptoms, and organ involvement such as hepatic injury) requiring immediate discontinuation, and hepatotoxicity (greater in hepatitis B/C co-infection or with immune reconstitution). An early safety signal suggested a small increased risk of neural tube defects with conception while on dolutegravir; subsequent data have shown the absolute risk is low, and current guidance supports its use in pregnancy with informed discussion and adequate folate. It interacts with polyvalent-cation antacids/supplements (separate dosing), metformin, and enzyme inducers (which may require twice-daily dosing). Renal dose adjustment is not required; it is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents in adults and pediatric patients (weight/age per product labeling)
Available as a single-tablet and as fixed-dose combinations (e.g. with lamivudine, or with abacavir/lamivudine, or with rilpivirine for virologically suppressed switch)

dosage.c: With certain UGT1A/CYP3A inducers (efavirenz, fosamprenavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir, rifampin, carbamazepine etc.)
dosage.n: Increase to overcome reduced exposure; rifabutin does not require increase

dosage.c: INSTI resistance (certain substitutions) or suspected INSTI resistance
dosage.n: Take with food to enhance exposure; some resistance combinations reduce efficacy

dosage.d: Weight-band dosing (e.g. children >=20 kg often 50 mg once daily; lower weights use dispersible tablets per label)
dosage.t: Once daily (twice daily if with inducers)
dosage.n: Use age/weight-specific formulation and dose per labeling

admin: May be taken with or without food; take WITH food when using twice-daily dosing for INSTI resistance

Take dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing products (Al/Mg antacids, calcium or iron supplements, multivitamins, sucralfate); or take together with food for calcium/iron
Always use as part of a combination antiretroviral regimen - never as monotherapy
Do not stop abruptly without medical advice; counsel strict adherence to maintain suppression and the resistance barrier
Stop immediately and seek care for signs of hypersensitivity (rash with fever, blistering, mucosal lesions, facial swelling, eosinophilia, organ dysfunction)
Discuss pregnancy planning and folate supplementation in those who may become pregnant
moa: Dolutegravir inhibits HIV-1 integrase, the viral enzyme required to insert (integrate) reverse-transcribed viral DNA into the host cell genome. It binds the integrase active site and blocks the strand-transfer step of the integration process, an essential step in the HIV-1 replication cycle. Preventing integration stops establishment of the provirus and downstream viral replication. As a second-generation INSTI, it has a high genetic barrier to resistance, retaining activity against many HIV strains with first-generation INSTI (raltegravir/elvitegravir) resistance substitutions.

absolute: Co-administration with dofetilide (dolutegravir inhibits its renal tubular secretion, risking serious/life-threatening arrhythmia)
relative: Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) - not recommended
Hepatitis B or C co-infection (higher risk of hepatotoxicity/immune reconstitution)
Use with strong UGT1A1/CYP3A inducers (need dose adjustment)
Women planning pregnancy or in early pregnancy (discuss neural-tube-defect signal and folate)
monitor: Hypersensitivity reactions (rash, constitutional and organ-specific signs)
Liver function, especially in hepatitis B/C co-infection
HIV-1 RNA and CD4 count (virologic/immunologic response)
Serum creatinine (early non-progressive rise from reduced tubular secretion - not true GFR decline)

preg: Dolutegravir is effective in pregnancy and is recommended in many guidelines. An initial surveillance signal suggested a small increase in neural tube defects when conception occurred on dolutegravir; with accumulated data the absolute excess risk is now considered low. Discuss this with patients of childbearing potential, ensure adequate folic acid, and individualize the choice; dolutegravir is generally continued or initiated during pregnancy with informed consent. Monitor as for any antiretroviral in pregnancy.
lact: Dolutegravir is present in human milk. In settings where formula feeding is safe and feasible, women with HIV are generally advised not to breastfeed to avoid HIV transmission. Where breastfeeding is recommended for other reasons, follow current national/WHO guidance. Counsel according to local recommendations.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in mild, moderate, or severe renal impairment in treatment-naive or INSTI-naive patients; it has not been studied in patients on dialysis. Dolutegravir reduces tubular secretion of creatinine, causing a small, early, non-progressive rise in serum creatinine without affecting actual glomerular filtration.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A or B). Dolutegravir is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) as it has not been studied. Monitor liver enzymes, especially in patients co-infected with hepatitis B or C.

major: Dofetilide - contraindicated; dolutegravir raises dofetilide levels with risk of serious arrhythmia

Polyvalent cations (Al/Mg-containing antacids, calcium, iron, multivitamins, sucralfate) - chelate dolutegravir and markedly reduce absorption; separate dosing (2 h before or 6 h after) or take with food for calcium/iron

Strong UGT1A1/CYP3A inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, efavirenz, etravirine without boosted PI, St John's wort, tipranavir/ritonavir, fosamprenavir/ritonavir) - reduce dolutegravir levels; increase to 50 mg twice daily or avoid
Metformin - dolutegravir increases metformin exposure; limit/adjust metformin dose and monitor
moderate: Etravirine alone - reduces dolutegravir; use only with a boosted PI
Rifabutin - modest reduction; no dose change needed
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food increases exposure and is recommended when twice-daily dosing for INSTI resistance, and can be used to take with calcium/iron supplements.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction with alcohol is described.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes an early, mild, reversible increase in serum creatinine (and decrease in estimated CrCl) by inhibiting tubular creatinine secretion - this does NOT reflect a true decline in glomerular filtration.

serious: Hypersensitivity reactions (rash with fever, constitutional symptoms, organ dysfunction including hepatic injury)
Depression and suicidal ideation (especially with pre-existing psychiatric illness)
rare: Neural tube defects with periconception exposure (small absolute risk signal)
emergency: Hypersensitivity reaction with organ involvement (rash, fever, blistering, facial swelling, hepatic injury)

monitoring: HIV-1 RNA (viral load) and CD4 count to assess response
Liver function tests, particularly in hepatitis B or C co-infection (and for hypersensitivity-related hepatic injury)
Signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity reactions
Serum creatinine (interpret the early small rise as reduced tubular secretion, not true renal decline)
Mood/psychiatric status in patients with pre-existing depression
Weight and metabolic parameters; pregnancy status and folate in those of childbearing potential
counsel: Take this medicine every day exactly as prescribed, as part of your full HIV combination - never skip doses, to keep the virus controlled and prevent resistance
Separate it from antacids, calcium, iron, or multivitamins - take dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after, or take iron/calcium together with food
Stop the medicine and get medical help right away if you develop a rash with fever, blisters, mouth sores, facial swelling, or yellowing of the skin/eyes
Tell your doctor if you feel very low in mood or have thoughts of harming yourself
If you can become pregnant, discuss this medicine with your doctor and take folic acid; do not stop without advice
It can be taken with or without food; tell your doctor about all other medicines and supplements you take
pk: Antiviral effect within days; meaningful viral-load decline over the first weeks
Plasma Tmax about 2-3 hours after an oral dose
Maintains suppression with once-daily dosing (twice-daily in defined situations)
Store at room temperature (~20-25 C) in the original container, protected from moisture
pearls: Second-generation INSTI with a HIGH barrier to resistance - a cornerstone of first-line HIV regimens (often as dolutegravir/lamivudine or with TDF/3TC)
HYPERSENSITIVITY (rash + systemic/organ involvement) and hepatotoxicity require immediate discontinuation - higher hepatic risk with hepatitis B/C
NEURAL-TUBE-DEFECT signal at conception was an early concern; absolute risk is low - use in pregnancy with informed discussion and folate
Separate from polyvalent cations (antacids, calcium, iron, multivitamins) - they chelate and reduce absorption
Causes a benign early rise in serum creatinine (blocks tubular creatinine secretion) - NOT true renal impairment; no renal dose change needed
Increase to 50 mg TWICE daily with strong UGT1A1/CYP3A inducers (e.g. rifampin, efavirenz) and with INSTI resistance; contraindicated with dofetilide; raises metformin levels
missed: If you miss a dose and it is more than 4 hours before your next scheduled dose, take the missed dose as soon as you remember, then continue your regular schedule. If it is within 4 hours of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one on time. Never take two doses at once. Consistent adherence is essential to prevent resistance.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for dolutegravir overdose; experience is limited. Management is supportive, including monitoring of clinical status and vital signs and standard symptomatic care. Because dolutegravir is highly protein-bound, dialysis is unlikely to remove significant amounts. Observe for adverse effects and treat as indicated.
